need.text: Qualification floor: waivers and MOC approvals require a recorded qualification on the person in addition to the role right.

acceptance.statement: The kernel exports approvalDecision and approvalAllowed.
CONTRACT.md records the assumption taken, the one open question, and the refused inputs.

check.run: grep -qi assumption /in/compose/CONTRACT.md && grep -qi question /in/compose/CONTRACT.md && grep -qi refus /in/compose/CONTRACT.md

acceptance.statement: A person with the role right but no recorded qualification for the action is never allowed, for both waivers and MOC approvals.

check.criteria: tests.json contains, for both waiver and MOC, a case with the role right and a missing or wrong-action qualification that expects denial (code 2 / false), and the kernel logic agrees.

acceptance.statement: A person with a qualification but without the role right is never allowed (the qualification does not replace the role right).

check.criteria: tests.json contains cases with a valid qualification and no role right expecting denial (code 1 / false), for both actions.

acceptance.statement: Approval is allowed only when both the role right and a recorded, unexpired qualification for that specific action are present.

check.criteria: tests.json includes allowed cases (code 0 / true) for both actions, the expiry boundary day (valid until == decision day), and an expired case (code 3 / false).

acceptance.statement: Malformed inputs (unknown action type, non 0/1 role flag, negative mask, non-finite days) trap rather than return a decision.

check.criteria: tests.json has expected-trap cases for each refused input class listed in CONTRACT.md, and glue.json carries a trap message for each.

acceptance.statement: glue.json carries labels, units, codes, the assumption and the question for both exports, and gates G1-G7 pass.

check.criteria: The compose gate report shows G1-G7 passing and glue.json has entries for approvalDecision and approvalAllowed including the assumption and question text matching CONTRACT.md.

atoms.title: Interface stub
atoms.contract: A markdown stub listing exact export names, argument names and order, types, units, decision codes and return types for approvalDecision and approvalAllowed, with no logic.

outputs.name: interface
outputs.describe: Export signatures, argument semantics, units, return codes.

atoms.verify: File exists and mentions approvalDecision, approvalAllowed, actionType, roleRight, qualMask, validUntilDay, decisionDay and codes 0,1,2,3.

worker.prompt: Write the interface stub. Exports: approvalDecision(actionType:i32, roleRight:i32, qualMask:i32, validUntilDay:f64, decisionDay:f64):i32 returning 0 allowed, 1 denied no role right, 2 denied no recorded qualification for the action, 3 denied qualification expired; and approvalAllowed(same arguments):i32 returning 1 if allowed else 0. actionType 1 = waiver, 2 = MOC approval. roleRight is 0/1. qualMask is the person's recorded qualification bits (bit0 value 1 = waiver approval qualification, bit1 value 2 = MOC approval qualification). Days are day numbers (days, any common epoch). Describe only the interface.

atoms.title: CONTRACT.md
atoms.contract: CONTRACT.md stating what is computed, the assumption taken for open facts, the one question that resolves it, and which inputs are refused (trap).
atoms.verify: File contains headings or words: computed, assumption, question, refused; mentions all four decision codes and check order role right, then qualification, then expiry.

worker.prompt: Write CONTRACT.md for the qualification floor on waiver and MOC approvals. Computed: approval requires the role right AND a recorded qualification on the person for that specific action. Check order: role right missing -> code 1; qualification bit for the action missing -> code 2; validUntilDay < decisionDay -> code 3 (equal is still valid); else 0. Assumption: the request does not say which qualification applies to which action, or whether qualifications expire; assume one qualification bit per action (1 waiver, 2 MOC) and a single valid-until day for the qualification. One question: which specific recorded qualification(s) does each of waiver and MOC approval require, and do they expire? Refused (trap): actionType not 1 or 2, roleRight not 0 or 1, qualMask negative, validUntilDay or decisionDay not finite. Do not invent facts about equipment.

atoms.title: Kernel: approvalDecision
atoms.contract: AssemblyScript source exporting approvalDecision per the interface and contract, returning codes 0-3 in the stated check order and trapping on refused inputs; helpers prefixed kernel-decision style (kernel_decision_).
atoms.verify: asc compiles it standalone; export approvalDecision present; no imports; all private names start with kernel_decision_.

worker.prompt: Implement approvalDecision from the interface and contract. Prefix every private helper or constant with kernel_decision_. Refused inputs trap via unreachable/abort-free throw as the procedure says.

atoms.title: Kernel: approvalAllowed
atoms.contract: AssemblyScript source exporting approvalAllowed per the interface and contract, returning 1 only when approvalDecision would return 0, else 0, trapping on the same refused inputs; self-contained, helpers prefixed kernel_allowed_.
atoms.verify: asc compiles it standalone; export approvalAllowed present; no imports; all private names start with kernel_allowed_.

worker.prompt: Implement approvalAllowed self-contained (do not call approvalDecision; it lives in another part). Prefix every private helper or constant with kernel_allowed_.

atoms.title: Tests: approvalDecision outcomes
atoms.contract: tests.json fragment with executable calls to approvalDecision and expected codes covering allowed, no role right, no qualification, wrong-action qualification, expired, expiry boundary, for both actions.
atoms.verify: Valid JSON in the gate test format; at least 12 cases; every code 0-3 appears for both actionType 1 and 2.

worker.prompt: Write test cases for approvalDecision from the interface and contract only. Include check-order cases (no role right and no qualification -> 1) and a qualMask holding both bits.

atoms.title: Tests: approvalAllowed outcomes
atoms.contract: tests.json fragment with executable calls to approvalAllowed and expected 0/1 covering every decision path of the contract for both actions.
atoms.verify: Valid JSON in the gate test format; at least 8 cases; includes both 1 and 0 results for each action.

worker.prompt: Write test cases for approvalAllowed from the interface and contract only.

atoms.title: Tests: refused inputs trap
atoms.contract: tests.json fragment with expected-trap calls to both exports for each refused input class: actionType 0/3, roleRight 2/-1, negative qualMask, NaN and Infinity days.
atoms.verify: Valid JSON in the gate test format; every case expects a trap; each refused class appears for both exports.

worker.prompt: Write expected-trap tests for both exports from the interface and contract only.

atoms.title: Glue: approvalDecision
atoms.contract: glue.json fragment for approvalDecision: labels, units (day number, code), precision, the four code meanings, the assumption, the question, and a trap message per refused input.
atoms.verify: Valid JSON; contains codes 0-3 with texts, assumption and question text matching CONTRACT.md, and a trap message for each refused class.

worker.prompt: Write the glue entry for approvalDecision in plain technician language. Quote the assumption and question from the contract.

atoms.contract: glue.json fragment for approvalAllowed: labels, unit (yes/no flag), 1/0 meanings, the assumption, the question, and a trap message per refused input.
atoms.verify: Valid JSON; contains 1/0 meanings, assumption and question matching CONTRACT.md, and a trap message for each refused class.

worker.prompt: Write the glue entry for approvalAllowed in plain technician language. Quote the assumption and question from the contract.

atoms.title: Compose artefact and run gates
atoms.contract: Gathers kernel parts into kernel.ts, merges tests and glue fragments into tests.json and glue.json, copies CONTRACT.md, compiles and runs gates G1-G7, and reports pass/fail without altering part content.
atoms.verify: gates.json shows G1-G7 pass; kernel.ts exports both functions; tests.json contains all fragment cases.

worker.prompt: Assemble the artefact from the parts and run the gates. Report any failing gate with its output; do not edit kernel or test logic.
